decisions.executionNote: Establish a continuous elbow-up approach with the left arm. Mallet shaft is rotated relative to the reference; refine alignment from new views before descending.
Align the open left gripper with the mallet handle near its free end, rotating toward a downward grasp while keeping elbow-up continuity.
Wrist view places the handle ahead of the current grasp point. Advance along the shaft and lower slowly, keeping the fingers open for visual alignment.
Make a small lateral correction to center the handle between the fingers, then close. Retention will be checked during a cautious lift.
Allow the fingers to finish closing around the centered shaft, then begin a small vertical test lift without changing orientation.
Lift the retained mallet clear of the table and turn it toward the first red key, keeping the left hand in its workspace and the right arm parked.
Bring the mallet tip above the first (leftmost red) key with clearance, using translation and modest yaw while retaining the shaft.
Lower the mallet vertically onto the leftmost red key, keeping horizontal alignment fixed; inspect contact before the required lift.
Lift 4.2 cm clear of the red key, then translate one key-width right toward orange while maintaining mallet retention and left-arm workspace.
Strike the second orange key vertically, pause briefly at contact height, and lift the mallet 3.6 cm before proceeding right.
Move above the third yellow key after the second-key lift, then begin a controlled vertical descent. The handle remains visibly retained.
Complete the third yellow-key strike at the established contact height and lift vertically by 4.1 cm before moving to green.
Advance to the fourth green key with clearance, then descend vertically to contact. Keep the hand left of center and the mallet securely closed.
Finish the green-key contact and lift 4.5 cm. Turn the raised mallet toward the fifth cyan key while keeping the entire left arm on its side rather than crossing the midline.
Strike the fifth cyan key at the established contact height, then lift 3.6 cm. A small horizontal correction centers the tip before descent.
Raise for clearance and swing the mallet tip one key right to dark blue. Compensate the shaft rotation with a small hand translation so the left arm stays well left of center.
Center the tip slightly left on the sixth dark-blue key, strike vertically, pause at contact, and lift 3.6 cm before the next key.
Move the lifted mallet to the seventh purple key by a small yaw and compensated translation. Keep the left hand left of center, with the tip reaching right.
Strike the seventh purple key with a vertical descent, then lift at least 3 cm before moving to the final magenta key.
Move the raised mallet above the eighth and final magenta key, maintaining the left hand on the left side and keeping the right arm parked.
Strike the final magenta key vertically, then lift the retained mallet by 4.8 cm, exceeding the required post-hit clearance.
The sequence has been attempted but completion is not confirmed. Raise well clear and return toward the first key to verify a full sequence with visibly established contacts.
Return the raised tip over the leftmost red bar. Recheck visual alignment and contact depth rather than assuming the earlier strokes registered.
Lower onto the first red key in small vertical increments and inspect the tip at contact before lifting. Earlier contact depth was uncertain.
The tip is visibly on the first red bar. Lift 5.5 cm before moving one key right to orange; use the newly observed contact depth for subsequent strokes.
Descend onto the second orange bar to the verified contact depth with a small margin, then inspect contact before lifting.
Lift clear of the visibly contacted orange bar, then move above yellow. Adjust the lateral spacing slightly to center the third stroke.
Center on the third yellow bar and descend to the observed contact level with a small margin. Pause for visual verification before the next lift.
Lift 5.5 cm from the visibly contacted yellow key, then move one bar right to green without sliding across the keys.
Descend vertically onto the fourth green bar to the verified contact depth, then pause for visual confirmation before lifting.
Lift clear of green by 5.5 cm, then position the tip over cyan using a modest yaw and hand compensation. Re-level the mallet after contact deflection; keep the left hand on its side.
Strike the fifth cyan key with a vertical descent to the established contact depth. Inspect the tip before lifting and advancing.
Lift 5.5 cm from cyan, then swing the raised tip to the sixth dark-blue bar with compensated hand translation, keeping the left hand left of center.
Strike the sixth dark-blue bar vertically at the verified contact depth. Pause to inspect the tip while keeping the shaft firmly retained.
Lift 5.5 cm from the visibly contacted sixth key, then move the raised mallet above the seventh purple bar while keeping the left hand left of center.
Strike the seventh purple key vertically to the established contact depth, pausing for visual verification before the required lift.
Lift 5.5 cm from the contacted purple bar, then place the raised tip over the final magenta bar with modest yaw and translation, leaving the hand left of center.
Strike the eighth magenta bar vertically to the established contact depth and pause. The final required lift follows after observing contact.
